title: Avila's acceleration via zeros of determinants and applications to Schrödinger cocycles
reviewed_version: arXiv:2212.05988v2, 4 January 2023, 22 pages; journal full text not compared
summary: The nonresonance index in the proof of Lemma6.5 can equal zero for two permitted I1 indices; its printed arithmetic bound is false. A corrected capacity count recovers the intended lemma under its covering hypotheses. Incorrect signs in (2.8) affect signed identities but not the subsequent magnitude estimates. Exponent relabeling is separately recorded as NeedsEvidence. No principal final theorem is disproved.
limitations: Every source page was read as text, but not all external large-deviation, avalanche, global-theory or spectral-theory dependencies were independently proved.
No complete independent reconstruction of the Section7 IDS transfer from GS2.
Journal version 79(3),729–761 was not compared with the acquired 22-page preprint.
No claim that an arbitrary interval in the arithmetic diagnostic equals the actual determinant-generated covering interval.
No author code executed and no missing code treated as a defect.
No independent acceptance or human review.

problems.title: The sum index in Lemma6.5 need not be large
problems.affected_object: A false arithmetic bound in a core derivation; not a demonstrated false lemma conclusion or final theorem

source_locator.statement: Lemma6.5 proof, assertion n/4<=l1+l2+n<=11n and its application of phase nonresonance
dependencies: Fact6.1 p.15; Lemma6.2 pp.16–18 paired cover

assumptions_verified: n=8m+1 with integer m>=1 can be arbitrarily large; y=2n satisfies n<y<10n.
I1=[-7m,-m] contains distinct l1=-4m+1 and l2=-4m-1.
theta=0 satisfies the stated eventual phase nonresonance for any allowed alpha and any fixed c'>0,b>1, because the strong Diophantine lower bound eventually dominates c'/|k|^b.
The resonance index l1+l2+n-1 is exactly zero; a large-|k| hypothesis cannot be invoked there.
The analytic/even-potential and first-supercritical-stratum conditions are retained in the conditional proof context, but the disproved index calculation is independent of f and E.
No actual spectral counterexample or determinant-generated U is claimed.
problems.check: For all m>=1 the claimed sum is1<n/4, and the two orbit points at theta0 are exact mates under x->-(n-1)alpha-x. Exact symbolic and integer computations are retained.
problems.result: The printed deterministic arithmetic assertion and resulting uniform one-point-per-pair justification are invalid.
counterevidence: A pair can contain at most two I1 points, at most one I2 point, and no points from both groups under the same arithmetic assumptions.
This improved count requires at least #I1/2+#I2=9n/8-O(1) pairs if every orbit point is covered; N''<=n+o(n) gives the needed contradiction.
The sign in the lemma statement differs from its proof; analysis uses the negative reflection consistently specified by Lemma6.2, so the sign typo is not counted separately.
No separate correction was located in the bounded public metadata/version checks; journal text was not examined.
problems.core_dependency: The good index from Lemma6.5, exclusion of I1 in Lemma6.6, and Corollary6.7 feed (6.67) and Theorem1.6.
problems.severity_reason: Demonstrated invalid step directly in the new localization derivation; local repair does not turn that step into a valid proof as printed.

repair.statement: Retain exponentially short pairs, allow capacity2 for I1-only pairs and capacity1 for I2-only pairs; rule out mixed pairs via sum index comparable to n. Their disjoint capacity yields #I1/2+#I2>n+o(n).
repair.boundaries: Conditional on the analytic cover and its cardinality. Does not certify every other lemma or disprove any final theorem.

independent_verification.claim_fidelity: Theorem 1.6 assumes an even analytic potential, strongly Diophantine alpha and theta outside an eventual resonant limsup set; this permits theta=0 and does not rule out the zero reflection index. Lemma 6.5 uses the false lower bound on indices in I1âˆªI2.
independent_verification.independent_argument: Set n=8m+1, y=2n, l1=-4m+1 and l2=-4m-1. Both lie in I1=[-7m,-m], l1+l2+n=1<n/4, and l1+l2+n-1=0. At theta=0 the intended opposite-component phase is exactly zero. Strong Diophantinity permits theta=0 outside the stated limsup because k^(b-1)/(log k)^a grows without bound. This refutes the uniform index step, without constructing the actual determinant cover or refuting localization.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The statement/proof reflection-sign discrepancy is separated from the substantive index failure. Same-component separation remains valid; mixed I1/I2 and two-I2 reflection indices stay nonzero of order n and are excluded by the phase assumption.
independent_verification.repair_verification: Each paired cover can hold at most two I1 points or one I2 point, with no mixed pair. Thus covering all points requires at least |I1|/2+|I2|=9n/8-O(1) pairs, more than n+o(n). This conditional capacity argument repairs the counting conclusion given the preceding analytic cover. It does not repair that analytic cover's exponent bookkeeping automatically.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_grade: Lemma 6.5 supplies the good-orbit-point argument used in Lemma 6.6, Corollary 6.7 and (6.67) in the proof of Theorem 1.6. The invalid core derivation supports Major despite a local counting repair. No claim that the final localization theorem is false.

problems.title: Finite-interval signed determinant identities use inconsistent signs
problems.affected_object: Signed expansion (2.8), not its absolute-value estimate
assumptions_verified: f=0 is real analytic and even.
E=3 and any frequency satisfying the stated Diophantine condition.
The formal recurrence solution phi[-1]=0,phi[0]=1 gives phi[1]=3,phi[2]=8.
The [0,1] restriction has determinant8 and is invertible.
Identity (2.8) is stated for solutions; no polynomial bound is required for this local identity.
This solution is not polynomially bounded, and E3 is outside the free spectrum, so it is not an Anderson-localization counterexample.
problems.check: Exact inverse of [[-3,1],[1,-3]] applied to [0,-8] is[1,3]; printed formula gives -1 at y0. General three-site symbolic cofactor columns independently checked.
problems.result: Incorrect pointwise signed identity under the printed determinant convention.
counterevidence: Correct alternating cofactor signs leave all subsequent absolute-value bounds unchanged.
Changing to det(E-H) is possible but needs two plus signs in the solution formula; convention change alone does not validate the printed two-minus formula.
problems.core_dependency: Used at (6.66), but only through absolute values; u_n<=v_n also survives corresponding transfer-matrix sign correction.
problems.severity_reason: Local identity error; no demonstrated damage to principal magnitude estimates.

repair.statement: Use alternating signs (-1)^(y-l1+1) and (-1)^(l2-y+1) in the two boundary terms for det(H-E). Correct transfer matrix accordingly.
repair.boundaries: Magnitude-based localization estimates remain available; no global theorem falsity claimed.

independent_verification.claim_fidelity: The source defines D_n=det(H-E), but prints a finite-interval identity with two uniform negative signs. Its scope includes formal solutions on an invertible finite interval, so the finite algebraic example is admissible for that identity.
independent_verification.independent_argument: For f=0,E=3, phi[-1]=0,phi[0]=1, recurrence gives phi[1]=3,phi[2]=8. On [0,1], H-E=[[-3,1],[1,-3]], D1=-3,D2=8. At y=0 the printed expression yields -1, whereas the actual value is 1. Cofactor expansion gives boundary signs (-1)^(y-l1+1) and (-1)^(l2-y+1). The corresponding transfer matrix under det(H-E) is (-1)^n [[Dn,D(n-1)(theta+alpha)],[-D(n-1)(theta),-D(n-2)(theta+alpha)]].
independent_verification.counterevidence: E=3 for the free operator is not offered as a spectral or polynomially bounded localization counterexample. Switching to det(E-H) would require two plus signs in the boundary formula, so it does not validate the printed convention.
independent_verification.repair_verification: Restoring the cofactor signs fixes the exact finite identity. The absolute-value estimates used in (2.6) and (6.66) are unchanged.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_grade: This is a genuine local signed-identity error with no demonstrated damage to the subsequent magnitude estimates; Minor is appropriate.

problems.title: The bad-set threshold needs an explicit exponent change
problems.affected_object: Unjustified identification of thresholds as printed; possible intended relabeling
assumptions_verified: delta>0 denotes the fixed exponent from Lemma2.6; C1>0 is fixed and n sufficiently large.
C1*n^(-delta/2) exceeds n^(-delta) for all sufficiently large n.
The smaller bad set handled by Lemma6.4 is not automatically a cover theorem for the larger bad set defined in (6.47).
problems.check: Exact scalar threshold comparison; explicit alternate gamma=delta/4 bookkeeping derived.
problems.result: Literal implication between the two conditions is unsupported by Lemma6.4 alone. No constructed determinant counterexample to Lemma6.2 or to a final theorem.
counterevidence: The weaker exponent in (6.64) suggests intended relabeling.
Retaining original delta for LDT/Cartan and defining a new bad set with gamma=delta/4 yields an applicable threshold and exponentially small arcs; downstream needs only o(1) loss.
A stronger estimate for the original set could also resolve the issue, but was not independently established.
problems.core_dependency: Lemma6.2 supplies the paired small-interval cover used in Lemma6.5 and localization.
problems.severity_reason: Recorded as NeedsEvidence rather than an additional confirmed Major because the admissible intended exponent-loss reading is plausible and a false final statement has not been established.

repair.statement: Retain delta in the initial LDT and Cartan proof; define Bhat={u_n<L_n-n^(-gamma)}, gamma=delta/4. Then n^(-gamma)>C1*n^(-delta/2), and O(n^-1 exp(-n^(delta/2)))<=exp(-n^gamma) for large n.
repair.boundaries: Repairs a new set definition. Does not establish the stronger cover for the original same-delta B_n.

independent_verification.claim_fidelity: The source defines Bn using n^(-gamma2), but Lemma 6.4 covers points below Ln-C1*n^(-gamma2/2); it then changes an arc exponent from gamma2/2 to gamma2 without an explicit relabeling.
independent_verification.independent_argument: For fixed delta>0, u=Ln-2*n^(-delta) belongs to the original bad set, yet for large n it does not satisfy u<Ln-C1*n^(-delta/2). This establishes a logical non-implication between scalar thresholds, not an actual determinant counterexample. The exponential arc claims also do not follow at their literal original exponents.
independent_verification.counterevidence: Equation (6.64) returns to the weaker gamma2/2 scale, supporting the possibility of intended exponent shrinking. The report correctly avoids asserting that the analytic theorem or literal inclusion has been disproved.
independent_verification.repair_verification: Keeping the original LDT exponent delta and defining a new bad-set exponent gamma=delta/4 makes n^(-gamma)>C1*n^(-delta/2) for large n, and O(n^(-1)*exp(-n^(delta/2)))<=exp(-n^gamma). The resulting smaller bad set is coverable and its complement still gives an Ln-o(1) determinant bound. This is a consistent revised formulation, not proof of the originally printed inclusion.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_grade: A missing exponent reconciliation affects the printed route but may be a harmless implicit shrink; NeedsEvidence preserves that uncertainty.

additional_checks.result: Annular radial Green average independently satisfies both boundary values, continuity, and derivative jump1.
Reciprocal zero pairing, monotonicity and Lyapunov slope support the 2n*kappa normalization; no issue established in this check.
additional_checks.scope: Not an independent proof of all imported bounds.
